verdict.summary: Use a Production OAuth 2.1 app for each end user's independent Calendly connection; do not use a personal access token for this multi-tenant model. Build and validate against a separate Sandbox app, then create a Production app with one HTTPS callback, PKCE, encrypted rotating refresh-token storage, and only the scopes the agent needs. There is no documented Production OAuth app review queue; user consent to requested scopes is the operative access gate.
verdict.activeEffort: 1–3 days, mostly implementing OAuth PKCE, encrypted token rotation, tenant-safe callback handling, and webhook verification (estimate)
verdict.waitTime: No documented review wait: the published setup material describes direct app creation and does not document a review queue or SLA.
verdict.mainGate: Each end user must consent to the requested OAuth scopes, and Production requires exactly one HTTPS redirect URI.

recommendation.text: Create separate Sandbox and Production OAuth apps. Use the authorization-code OAuth 2.1 flow with PKCE for each tenant user's connection, retain tokens only in server-side encrypted storage, and use the hosted MCP server only if Dynamic Client Registration—not manually issued console credentials—fits the product architecture.

sources.quote: OAuth is required for multiple accounts, while personal access tokens are used for installing in a single account at a time.
We recommend that you start with a Sandbox app for development. Create a second app for Production when you are ready to use real customer data.
❌ Manual OAuth app provisioning (console-issued credentials)

essentials.text: Access tokens expire after two hours. Keep refresh tokens only in encrypted server-side storage; refresh tokens are single-use, so serialize refreshes per connection and atomically store the replacement token after every successful refresh.

sources.quote: Access Tokens expire after 2 hours.
A refresh token is revoked immediately after a successful POST /oauth/token call.
Refresh tokens are handled only on the server side , in secure storage.

essentials.text: Register exactly one stable callback URI per OAuth app. Sandbox supports HTTPS and localhost HTTP; Production accepts HTTPS URIs only, and the token exchange must send the same redirect URI used to obtain the code.

sources.quote: Redirect URI : the URL where Calendly sends users after they authorize your app. Enter exactly one URI.
Production https URIs only
redirect_uri : the same redirect URI that you used to get the code

essentials.text: Create a separate Production OAuth app when handling real customer data, configure its single HTTPS callback, and securely save the client secret and webhook signing key during creation because they cannot be displayed again.

sources.quote: Environment type : select Sandbox for development and testing, or Production when your app is ready for real users.
Copy all three values and store them securely before you leave this screen. You cannot view the client secret or the webhook signing key again.

essentials.text: Not found in the sources researched

PKCE with S256 is mandatory for every OAuth app. Verify webhooks using HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp, a period, and the raw JSON body; reject stale deliveries, with Calendly's example using a three-minute tolerance.

sources.quote: Every OAuth app must use PKCE conforming to RFC 7636, with the S256 method.
# Determine the expected signature by computing an HMAC with the SHA256 hash function.
In the example below, the tolerance zone is set to 3 minutes, so any webhooks received that are older than 3 minutes will be rejected.

detail.text: Sign in to Calendly, open Profile menu → Developer → Developer tools, select Create, and choose Sandbox as the environment. Use this app only for integration development before registering a distinct Production app for customer data.

sources.quote: Open Developer tools . In Calendly, open the Profile menu and select Developer .
Environment type : select Sandbox for development and testing, or Production when your app is ready for real users.

steps.title: Set the single callback and preserve app secrets

detail.text: In the OAuth app Redirect URI field, enter one stable callback endpoint; use HTTPS for Production. Copy the client ID, client secret, and webhook signing key into the production secret manager before leaving the creation screen.

sources.quote: Redirect URI : the URL where Calendly sends users after they authorize your app. Enter exactly one URI.
Copy all three values and store them securely before you leave this screen. You cannot view the client secret or the webhook signing key again.

steps.title: Prepare the tenant-safe OAuth callback contract

detail.text: Implement the callback using a server-stored, single-use transaction bound to the tenant and user connection. Send response_type=code, the registered redirect URI, and an S256 PKCE challenge; at callback validate the transaction before exchanging the code with the same URI and verifier.

sources.quote: Redirect the user to Calendly’s authorization page with the client_id , redirect_uri , and code_challenge
If the request does not include a code_challenge , it fails.
If your app runs on a server, also send your client secret. Use HTTP Basic authentication with your client ID as the username and your client secret as the password.

steps.title: Test consent, refresh rotation, and denied permissions

detail.text: Run the Sandbox acceptance checks against a test connection, including declined scope handling, single-use refresh-token rotation, webhook signature rejection, and per-user rate-limit backoff before creating Production credentials.

sources.quote: Confirm that the user granted all requested scopes (users can decline scopes during install).
A refresh token is revoked immediately after a successful POST /oauth/token call.
If you receive a 429 response, wait until the X-RateLimit-Reset time has elapsed before retrying.

steps.output:
Sandbox acceptance checks:
1. Authorize read-only scopes; confirm the tenant binding.
2. Decline one requested scope; show a reconnect message.
3. Refresh once; verify the old refresh token is unusable.
4. Force concurrent refresh attempts; permit one writer only.
5. Send a stale or altered webhook; reject it.
6. Confirm 429 retries wait for X-RateLimit-Reset.

detail.text: Do not wait for a documented OAuth app-review queue. Confirm internally that the Production app requests minimum scopes and that consent, data-use disclosures, and security controls are ready; then proceed to create the Production app.

steps.title: Register and deploy the Production OAuth app

detail.text: Create a second OAuth app with Environment type set to Production, configure the deployed HTTPS callback, store its new credentials separately from Sandbox, and enable the user connection flow with the minimum selected scopes.

sources.quote: We recommend that you start with a Sandbox app for development. Create a second app for Production when you are ready to use real customer data.

steps.title: Publish the data-use disclosure

detail.text: Prepare and publish a connection-screen disclosure that transparently states the collection, use, and sharing of Calendly customer data, including any sharing with AI service providers that applies to the workflow. Limit use of the data to the practices disclosed.

sources.quote: Use of customer data must be transparent by disclosing the collection, use and sharing of the data. You must limit your use of the data to the practices you disclose.

steps.output:
Draft disclosure for review:
“When you connect Calendly, we access only the permissions you approve to provide requested scheduling assistance. We process Calendly data to run the selected workflow and may send necessary data to our AI service providers. We do not use your connection for unrelated purposes. You can disconnect Calendly at any time.”
